chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When you bring the deceased to the grave, pull him in by his feet; so when you place him in the grave, recite Ayat al-Kursi.
And say: 'In the name of Allah, and in the way of Allah, and upon the religion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)'.
O Allah, expand for him in his grave and join him with his prophet (peace be upon him and his family).
And say, as you said during the prayer upon him, once:
From Allah, if he was a good doer, then increase in his goodness, and if he was an evil doer, then forgive him, have mercy on him, and overlook him.
And seek forgiveness for him as much as you are able.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And it was so that whenever Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) entered the deceased into the grave, he said: O Allah, turn the earth away from his sides, and ascend his deeds, and grant him pleasure from You'.

key_terms.آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ: Ayat al-Kursi (The Verse of the Throne, Quran 2:255)
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: Prayer (specifically Salat al-Mayyit or general supplication)
key_terms.جَافِ: Turn away / Keep away (referring to the earth)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications and actions when placing the deceased in the grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific etiquette of burial, emphasizing the physical handling of the body and the recitation of Ayat al-Kursi as a means of spiritual protection and honor. It highlights the Shia tradition of interceding for the deceased through targeted supplications, such as asking for 'fasc' (expansion) in the grave, reflecting the belief in the soul's intermediate state (Barzakh). The inclusion of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn’s distinct prayer underscores the continuity of prophetic family practices in guiding the community through the transition of death.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn AbuUmeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When they come with the deceased to the grave, so place him from the direction of his legs, So when you place him in the grace, recite Ayat Al Kursy (Chapter 2:255) and say, ‘In the Name of Allahazwj’, and say just as you said during the Salaat upon him, once in his presence, ‘O Allahazwj!
If he was a good doer, so Increase in his good deeds, and if he was an evil doer, so Forgive him, and be Merciful to him, and Overlook (his sins) from him’.
And seek Forgiveness for him , and Forgive him whatever whatever you are able to’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And it was so that whenever Ali Bin Al Husayn<sup>asws</sup> entered the deceased into the grave, said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Expand the ground from both his sides and Ascend his deeds, and Assign him the Pleasure from You<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following:
“Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that you should place a deceased, after his arrival near the grave, in it from the side where you intend to place his feet.
When the deceased is placed in the grave, read Ayatu al-Kursiy and say, ’(I begin) in the name of Allah, in the way of Allah and on the path of the Messenger of Allah.
O Allah, make his grave comfortably spacious and join him with his prophet, who with his family are ‘Alayhim al-Salam .’
Then say what you have just said in Salah (prayer) for the deceased only once nearby,
‘O Allah, if he is a person of good deed, increase his good deeds and if he is a person of bad deeds, please forgive him, have mercy on him and ignore his sins.’
You should ask forgiveness for him as much as possible.

The Imam said, ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn, Alayhi al-Salam, at the time of placing a deceased in the grave would say, “O Allah make his place spacious on both sides, accept his good deeds and grant him happiness from Your side.’””
